top_temples.name: Jagannath Temple, Bhilai
top_temples.location_note: Bhilai; major Rath Yatra celebrations draw thousands of devotees annually.

top_temples.name: Shree Shirdi Saibaba Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Sector 6, Bhilai; popular for its evening aarti gatherings.

top_temples.name: Maa Jagdamba Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Bhilai; heavily visited during Navratri.

top_temples.name: Shiva Mandir, Bhilai
top_temples.location_note: A roughly 400-year-old temple in Bhilai, one of the city's oldest.

top_temples.name: Ganga Maiya Temple, Bhilai
top_temples.location_note: Built in the 10th century by Chhattisgarh kings; blends Hindu and Buddhist architectural styles with a pyramid-like structure.

top_temples.name: Pataleshwar Cave Temple, Malhar
top_temples.location_note: Malhar village, Bilaspur district; 8th-century cave shrine carved from a single basalt rock during the Rashtrakuta dynasty.

top_temples.name: Devrani Jethani Temple Complex, Tala
top_temples.location_note: Tala village, Bilaspur district, on the Maniyari river; 5th-century twin temples built by the Sharabhapuriya dynasty, ASI-protected.

top_temples.name: Kali Mandir, Bilaspur
top_temples.deity: Kali, with halls for Vishnu, Shiva, Rama-Sita, Hanuman, and Krishna
top_temples.location_note: Bilaspur city; a multi-deity temple complex.

top_temples.name: Deur Temple, Malhar
top_temples.location_note: Malhar archaeological site, Bilaspur district; known for artistic idols.

top_temples.name: Dindeshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bilaspur district; dates to the 10th-11th century.

top_temples.name: Danteshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the confluence of the Shankini and Dhankini rivers in Dantewada; a 14th-century Shakti Peetha built by Kakatiya rulers, gives the town its name, month-long Dussehra festival.

top_temples.name: Bhairav Baba Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 2 km from the main Danteshwari Temple in Dantewada; a distinct shrine with ancient idols and statues dated to the 14th century and later.

top_temples.name: Bilai Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop near Madamsilli Dam, Dhamtari district; major Navratri fair.

top_temples.name: Rudreshwar Mahadev Temple, Rudri
top_temples.location_note: Rudri, near Dhamtari; a well-known local Shiva shrine in traditional Hindu architectural style.

top_temples.name: Maitri Bagh Shiv Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Durg city; known for detailed architectural carvings.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Temple, Durg
top_temples.location_note: In the heart of Durg city.

top_temples.name: Balaji Dham
top_temples.location_note: On the outskirts of Durg city.

top_temples.name: Deorbijia Temple
top_temples.location_note: Deorbijia village near Durg; especially visited during Shivratri.

top_temples.name: Ganga Maiya Temple, Jhalmala
top_temples.location_note: Jhalmala, near Durg; heavily visited during festivals.

top_temples.name: Narayanpal Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Indravati River near Jagdalpur; built in the 11th century, known for intricate carvings.

top_temples.name: Jagannath Temple, Jagdalpur
top_temples.location_note: Jagdalpur city, near Mawli Mata Temple; noted for its distinctive entrance.

top_temples.name: Mawli Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: A revered cave temple amid forests near Jagdalpur, closely tied to the city's Dussehra festival.

top_temples.name: Ganesha Temple, Barsur
top_temples.location_note: Barsur, about 75 km from Jagdalpur on the Indravati river; part of an ancient complex of 147 temples, features an 8-ft-high, 17-ft-wide Ganesha idol.

top_temples.name: 32-Pillar Shiva Temple, Barsur
top_temples.location_note: Barsur, within the same temple complex as the Ganesha temple, distinct structure with a black Nandi statue.

top_temples.name: Sarvamangala Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Hasdeo River, Korba; surrounded by Trilokinath Mandir, Kali Mandir, and Jyoti Kalash Bhavan.

top_temples.name: Dakshin Mukhi Hanuman Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Korba town; a prominent religious landmark.

top_temples.name: Mandwarani Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop a hill at about 3,060 ft near Korba, offering panoramic views.

top_temples.name: Chakreshwar Mahadev Temple, Kanki
top_temples.location_note: Kanki, about 20 km from Korba; a highly sanctified shrine.

top_temples.name: Sitamani Temples and Caves
top_temples.location_note: Near Korba; three rock-cut caves housing ancient idols.

top_temples.name: Pahadi Mandir, Raigarh
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple in Raigarh, reached via a long stairway trek.

top_temples.name: Balaji Temple, Raigarh
top_temples.location_note: Raigarh district; built in 1610 by Shri Balbhadra Dasji and Shri Bhosleji.

top_temples.name: Barfani Dham, Raigarh
top_temples.location_note: Raigarh; noted for an ice-formed Shiva linga resilient to summer heat.

top_temples.name: Mankeshwari Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Raigarh district.

top_temples.name: Sarangarh Mahamaya Temple
top_temples.location_note: Sarangarh, Raigarh district; a locally notable Devi shrine.

top_temples.name: Maa Mahamaya Devi Temple, Raipur
top_temples.location_note: Raipur's oldest temple; major Navratri and Durga Puja destination, distinct from the Ratanpur/Bilaspur Mahamaya shrine.

top_temples.name: Sri Jagannath Mandir, Raipur
top_temples.location_note: One of Raipur's most visited temples, known for its Mahaprasad.

top_temples.name: Shri Ram Mandir, Raipur
top_temples.location_note: Raipur city; blends modern and traditional architectural design.

top_temples.name: Banjari Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: One of Raipur's oldest Devi shrines.

top_temples.name: Shree Khatu Shyam Mandir, Raipur
top_temples.location_note: A well-known temple within Raipur city.

top_temples.name: Rajiv Lochan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rajim's central shrine, dated to the 8th century CE, at the confluence of the Mahanadi, Pairi, and Sondur rivers, giving Rajim its name 'Prayag of Chhattisgarh'.

top_temples.name: Kuleshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Rajim, close to the Rajiv Lochan Temple, on the riverbank.

top_temples.name: Maa Bamleshwari Temple, Dongargarh
top_temples.location_note: Dongargarh, Rajnandgaon district; hilltop temple reached via 1,000 steps, one of Chhattisgarh's most visited shrines.

top_temples.name: Paatal Bhairavi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rajnandgaon; a three-tiered temple with Bhairavi below, Navadurga in the middle, and a large Shiva statue above.

top_temples.name: Barfani Dham, Rajnandgaon
top_temples.location_note: Rajnandgaon district; features large statues of Shiva and Nandi.

top_temples.name: Mata Sheetala Devi Shakti Peetha
top_temples.location_note: Dongargarh, Rajnandgaon district; a notable Shakti shrine distinct from the Bamleshwari temple.

top_temples.name: Chandrahasini Devi Temple, Chandkhuri
top_temples.location_note: Chandkhuri village, Rajnandgaon district; a well-known regional Devi shrine.

top_temples.name: Mahamaya Devi Temple (Kosaleswari Devi Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Ratanpur's central shrine, built by King Ratna Dev of the Kalachuri dynasty; one of the 52 Shakti Peethas, historic Kalachuri capital.

top_temples.name: Ram Tekri Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Atop the Ram Tekri hill in Ratanpur; built by Maratha king Shivaji Rao Bhonsle, features granite statues.

top_temples.name: Lakshman Temple
top_temples.location_note: Sirpur's central shrine; one of India's earliest surviving brick temples, dated to the 6th-7th century CE, commissioned by Vasata, mother of ruler Mahashivagupta Balarjuna.

top_temples.name: Gandheshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Overlooking the Mahanadi river in Sirpur; built atop ancient temple and vihara ruins, the only Shiva linga among Sirpur's many still actively worshipped, said to emit a natural fragrance each morning.
